title: Rebase copies; it does not move
brief:
This is the Act 4 cliff, so: observation first. `feature` forked from main one commit ago. Meanwhile main moved. You want feature's work to sit on top of the NEW main, in a straight line, with no merge commit.

`git rebase main` (run while ON feature) replays feature's commits one by one onto main's tip. Read that again: replays. Each replayed commit is a brand new commit object with a new hash. The originals stay in the object store, abandoned, faded on the graph.

Do it: switch to feature and rebase it onto main. Then look at the graph and find the ghost.

goals.label: The feature work survived the replay
Three commits: initial, main moves, feature work

diagnostics.say: Rebase moves the branch you are ON. Get onto feature first: git switch feature.

hints: git switch feature, then git rebase main.
If you rebased while on main, git answered 'up to date': main is already based on itself. Switch first.
Merging main INTO feature would also combine them, but with a merge commit and the lines crossed. Rebase makes the straight line.
